question: Do the tests added for the Issue #307 sibling-directory tier (scripts/test-verify-stages.ps1, section "Issue #307: convention-based resolution when the environment is not inherited") catch three independent regressions - the tier missing, the tier ordered ahead of GODOT4_CONSOLE, and the tier accepting any version - each on its own distinct assertion?
method: Applied one mutation at a time to the committed scripts/GodotTools.ps1 (verified clean via 'git status --short' before each), ran 'powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/test-verify-stages.ps1' (which exercises the new fixture directly and, through its own engine-gate smoke check, a nested 'verify.ps1 -Stage scripts'), recorded the failing assertion text and exit code, then restored the committed file with 'git checkout -- scripts/GodotTools.ps1' before the next mutation.

mutants.name: A: remove the sibling-directory tier entirely

diff.find:
# Issue #307. Last resort, and deliberately last: the three tiers above all
    # read from this process's own environment (-GodotPath is the caller's
    # argument, GODOT4_CONSOLE and PATH are inherited variables), and a machine
    # can have every one of them set correctly while this particular process
    # still sees none of it - measured in evidence/307-resolution.json, where
    # GODOT4_CONSOLE and the PATH entry both existed at User scope but neither
    # reached the agent's process tree, which had forked before they were
    # written. A directory laid out next to the repository root the way
    # ENVIRONMENT_SETUP.md documents is read straight off disk instead, so it
    # survives that gap on any machine using the documented layout - with no
    # environment variable, and without this repository writing one either
    # (AGENTS.md forbids that).
    #
    # $PSScriptRoot here is this file's own directory (scripts/), not the
    # caller's - PowerShell binds it to where a function is *defined*, not
    # where it is invoked from, confirmed for run-game.ps1, verify.ps1 and
    # spikes/142-scale-spike/capture-scale-spike.ps1 alike. That makes the
    # repository root one Join-Path away, the same computation verify.ps1
    # itself uses for $repoRoot.
    $repositoryRoot = [IO.Path]::GetFullPath((Join-Path $PSScriptRoot ".."))
    $parentDirectory = Split-Path -Parent $repositoryRoot

    if (-not [string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($parentDirectory) -and
        (Test-Path -LiteralPath $parentDirectory -PathType Container)) {

        # Sorted newest-version-first by directory name, so that when more than
        # one such directory exists side by side - as this repository's own
        # development machine does, with a 4.6.1 and a 4.7.1 checkout both
        # present - the tier prefers the higher version instead of whichever
        # one the filesystem happens to enumerate first. This is a preference,
        # not a correctness filter: a lone wrong-version directory is still
        # returned (there is nothing else to return), so Assert-GodotVersion
        # is the one that rejects it and names the version it found, exactly
        # as it already does for every other tier above.
        $candidateDirectories = @(
            Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $parentDirectory -Directory `
                -Filter "Godot_v*-stable_mono_win64" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
            Sort-Object -Property Name -Descending)

        foreach ($candidateDirectory in $candidateDirectories) {
            $consoleExecutable = Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $candidateDirectory.FullName `
                -Filter "*_console.exe" -File -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
                Select-Object -First 1
            if ($null -ne $consoleExecutable) {
                return [IO.Path]::GetFullPath($consoleExecutable.FullName)
            }
        }
    }

    throw @"

mutants.note: Verified separately (not assumed) that Get-ChildItem's own unsorted enumeration order over the fixture's two junctioned directories is 'Godot_v4.6.1-stable_mono_win64' then 'Godot_v4.7.1-stable_mono_win64' - alphabetical, not creation order - so removing Sort-Object -Descending deterministically flips the picked candidate to the wrong version rather than accidentally still passing.

conclusion: All three mutants turn scripts/test-verify-stages.ps1 red, and each dies on a different assertion: A on 'did not resolve at all' (Success = $false), B on 'the explicit override lost priority' (wrong Source/path even though Success = $true), C on 'resolved successfully but to the wrong version' (Success = $true, path is the 4.6.1 sibling instead of the 4.7.1 one). No two mutants share their failing assertion, so passing coverage is not an artifact of one shared check.
restoredCommittedStateBetweenMutants: git checkout -- scripts/GodotTools.ps1, verified with 'git status --short' producing no output before applying the next mutant and again after the last one.

reviewRound1.question: Independent review of PR #308 (major finding 1) found that these same three mutants, run against the pre-fix test harness, each left the Issue #307 sandbox (including its junctions to the real Godot_v4.7.1 and Godot_v4.6.1 installs) behind on disk under .artifacts, because the cleanup call sat after the checking block instead of in a finally. Fixed in commit c86d2d5 by wrapping the block in try/finally. This entry re-verifies, on the fixed test harness, that (a) the same three mutants still die on the same three distinct assertions, and (b) none of them leaves anything behind afterwards.

reviewRound1.preExistingLeftoversFoundAndCleared: Before this round's reruns, .artifacts/ still held eight verify-stage-guard-<guid> directories from this session's *original* (pre-fix) mutant runs, four of them containing live junctions to C:\gamedev\Godot_v4.7.1-stable_mono_win64 and C:\gamedev\Godot_v4.6.1-stable_mono_win64 - exactly what review reported. Verified with Get-ChildItem -Recurse | Where-Object LinkType that the entries were junctions (not copies) and that both real Godot install directories were intact and unaffected; removed all eight with Remove-Item -Recurse -Force before rerunning the mutants on the fixed harness.
reviewRound1.separateObservationOutOfScope: After each rerun on the fixed harness, an empty top-level '.artifacts/verify-stage-guard-<guid>' directory (and, for a mutant that fails before the nested 'verify.ps1 -Stage scripts' child completes, a second empty one from that child's own run) can still remain. These contain no junctions and no files - they are $sandbox itself, created near the top of test-verify-stages.ps1 and normally removed only by the unrelated 'guard against itself' try/finally at the very end of the file, which never runs if anything earlier throws. This is a pre-existing, file-wide pattern that predates this PR and is not what review's finding 1 was about (no reparse points involved, nothing outside .artifacts/); left unaddressed here as out of scope, called out in the PR comment for the coordinator to triage separately if wanted.
